features.name: Tirawa
features.description: Tirawa marks one of Rhea's great ancient impact scars. Its eroded basin rim and battered surroundings make it a useful landmark for reading how heavily the moon's icy crust was cratered early in Saturn-system history.

details.label: Diameter
details.value: Large basin; USGS center feature lists 0 km because the named point is used as the formal anchor.

details.label: Coordinate source
details.value: USGS Gazetteer center: 34.20 N, 151.70 W; app longitude remap: 180 - west.

details.label: Why it matters
details.value: NASA identifies Tirawa as the giant basin visible near Rhea's limb in late Cassini views, making it one of the moon's signature landmarks.

features.name: Mamaldi
features.description: Mamaldi is a broad, 480 km impact structure that sprawls across Rhea's cratered terrain. Its size makes it one of the best stops for comparing basin-scale impacts with smaller, sharper craters nearby.

details.label: Diameter
details.value: About 480 km

details.label: Coordinate source
details.value: USGS Gazetteer center: 14.00 N, 184.00 W; app longitude remap: 180 - west.

details.label: Name origin
details.value: Named for a Nanai creator goddess connected with the creation of the Asian continent and Sakhalin Island.

features.name: Inktomi
features.description: Inktomi is Rhea's bright young showpiece: a 47 km crater with rays of fresh icy ejecta spread across older terrain. Its crisp rays and strong water-ice signature help scientists study one of the more recent major impacts in Saturn's mid-sized moons.

details.label: Diameter
details.value: About 47 km

details.label: Coordinate source
details.value: USGS Gazetteer center: 14.10 S, 112.10 W; app longitude remap: 180 - west.

details.label: Fun Fact
details.value: Published age estimates place Inktomi among the youngest large craters in Saturn's regular moon system.

features.name: Powehiwehi
features.description: Powehiwehi is a huge crater on Rhea's darker trailing hemisphere. Its broad form helps show how the trailing side has been altered by magnetospheric particles while still preserving the old impact record.

details.label: Diameter
details.value: About 271 km

details.label: Coordinate source
details.value: USGS Gazetteer center: 8.20 S, 280.40 W; app longitude remap: 180 - west.

details.label: Name origin
details.value: Named for the first female being in Hawaiian myth, paired with Pouliuli.

features.name: Wakonda
features.description: Wakonda is a large northern crater that gives the explorer a high-latitude reference point away from the equatorial ray systems and trailing-hemisphere scarps.

details.label: Diameter
details.value: About 123 km

details.label: Coordinate source
details.value: USGS Gazetteer center: 48.60 N, 269.70 W; app longitude remap: 180 - west.

details.label: Name origin
details.value: Named for the Sioux great creator of all things.

features.name: Galunlati Chasmata
features.description: Galunlati Chasmata is one of the long fracture systems cutting across Rhea. These troughs and scarps are part of the wispy-looking terrain that hints at tectonic stresses in an otherwise quiet icy moon.

details.label: Length
details.value: About 740 km

details.label: Coordinate source
details.value: USGS Gazetteer center: 38.00 N, 290.00 W; app longitude remap: 180 - west.

details.label: Name origin
details.value: Named for the vault above the sky in Cherokee creation stories.

features.name: Avaiki Chasmata
features.description: Avaiki Chasmata traces a long set of grooves and scarps through Rhea's fractured hemisphere. It is a strong companion stop to Galunlati for showing that Rhea's surface is more than a static crater field.

details.label: Length
details.value: About 580 km

details.label: Coordinate source
details.value: USGS Gazetteer center: 25.00 N, 279.00 W; app longitude remap: 180 - west.

details.label: Name origin
details.value: Named for an underworld in Cook Islands mythology.

features.name: Puchou Catenae
features.description: Puchou Catenae is a long chain of aligned depressions. Catenae can record secondary impacts, structural weaknesses, or disrupted impactor fragments, making them useful clues to local surface history.

details.label: Length
details.value: About 620 km

details.label: Coordinate source
details.value: USGS Gazetteer center: 32.00 N, 87.00 W; app longitude remap: 180 - west.

details.label: Name origin
details.value: Named for a mountain in Chinese mythology connected with the tilting of Earth's axis.

features.name: Onokoro Catenae
features.description: Onokoro Catenae is a southern chain of pits and small craters that cuts across older terrain. Its aligned form gives Rhea's southern hemisphere a different texture from the broad basins and isolated craters.

details.label: Length
details.value: About 240 km

details.label: Coordinate source
details.value: USGS Gazetteer center: 44.70 S, 328.50 W; app longitude remap: 180 - west.

details.label: Name origin
details.value: Named for the island formed by a drop of water from the sword of Izanagi and Izanami.

features.name: Harahvaiti Fossa
features.description: Harahvaiti Fossa is a southern trough system. It gives the map a compact tectonic stop that contrasts with Rhea's longer chasmata and with the impact-dominated landscapes around Mamaldi.

details.label: Length
details.value: About 190 km

details.label: Coordinate source
details.value: USGS Gazetteer center: 36.00 S, 171.00 W; app longitude remap: 180 - west.

details.label: Name origin
details.value: Named for a beautiful land created by Ahura Mazda in Persian tradition.

features.name: Parun Fossa
features.description: Parun Fossa is a shorter trough south of the equator. Its placement near other southern features makes it a good marker for following Rhea's fractured terrain across the globe.

details.label: Length
details.value: About 120 km

details.label: Coordinate source
details.value: USGS Gazetteer center: 46.50 S, 152.00 W; app longitude remap: 180 - west.

details.label: Name origin
details.value: Named for a river in Nuristan tradition.

features.name: E-ring-coated Leading Hemisphere
features.description: Rhea's leading hemisphere is relatively bright because it is dusted by icy particles from Saturn's E ring, supplied by neighboring Enceladus. The contrast with the darker trailing side is one of the main color stories in the Cassini global map.

details.label: Coordinate note
details.value: Broad visual storytelling anchor, not an IAU named feature center.

details.label: Texture cue
details.value: NASA's PIA18438 notes the leading hemisphere is lighter while the trailing hemisphere is darker and altered by Saturn's magnetospheric environment.

details.label: Fun Fact
details.value: Rhea is far enough from Enceladus that the E-ring coating is subtler than on closer moons, but it still helps paint the global color pattern.

features.name: Dark Trailing Hemisphere
features.description: The trailing hemisphere carries darker, more radiation-processed colors than the leading side. This broad terrain stop helps connect Rhea's surface appearance to the plasma and particle environment inside Saturn's magnetosphere.

details.label: Coordinate note
details.value: Broad visual storytelling anchor, not an IAU named feature center.

details.label: Texture cue
details.value: The Cassini color map emphasizes the brightness and color difference between the two hemispheres.

details.label: Why it matters
details.value: Leading-trailing color asymmetry is a shared theme across several Saturnian icy moons, but each moon records it differently.
